kangaroo-ca-2019-g0304-01.title: Order the steps by height
kangaroo-ca-2019-g0304-01.body:
Runner D stands on the highest step, B on the second highest, E on the third highest, then C, and A stands lowest. So the order is D, B, E, C, A, and E finished third.

**Answer: (E) E**

kangaroo-ca-2019-g0304-01.title: Remove the top two
kangaroo-ca-2019-g0304-01.body:
Cover the highest step (D, first) and then the next highest (B, second). The highest step still visible is E's, so E is third.

**Answer: (E) E**

kangaroo-ca-2019-g0304-06.title: Look for each pair in the sheet
kangaroo-ca-2019-g0304-06.body:
The pieces show two upright symbols side by side, so we need two upright symbols next to each other in one row.

- (A) heart and diamond: no heart is next to a diamond in the right way. ✗
- (B) star and spade: the only other star (row 3) is tilted. ✗
- (C) two stars: the two stars are not neighbours. ✗
- (D) star and club: row 1 has the upright star next to an upright club. ✓
- (E) two hearts: the two upright hearts in the right column are on top of each other, not side by side; turning that piece would turn the hearts on their side. ✗

**Answer: (D)**

kangaroo-ca-2019-g0304-06.title: Start from the star
kangaroo-ca-2019-g0304-06.body:
There is only one upright star (row 1, column 2). Its right neighbour is an upright club, so the piece star–club can be cut out. That is (D).

**Answer: (D)**

kangaroo-ca-2019-g0304-07.title: Check from the bottom up
kangaroo-ca-2019-g0304-07.body:
We need, from bottom to top: 3 cubes, then 2 cylinders, then 1 cube.

- (A): 3 cubes at the bottom, 2 cylinders on them, 1 cube on top. ✓
- (B): only 1 cylinder at the top, and more cubes below. ✗
- (C): cylinders at the bottom. ✗
- (D): 2 cubes on top, not 1. ✗
- (E): 3 cubes at the top and 1 at the bottom — upside down. ✗

**Answer: (A)**

kangaroo-ca-2019-g0304-07.title: Count each kind
kangaroo-ca-2019-g0304-07.body:
Liam uses 4 cubes and 2 cylinders, with the cylinders in the middle layer. (B) has only one cylinder, (C) has the cylinders at the bottom, and (D) and (E) have the wrong number of cubes on top. Only (A) fits.

**Answer: (A)**

kangaroo-ca-2019-g0304-10.title: Size of the big cube
kangaroo-ca-2019-g0304-10.body:
The tower in the back corner is 3 cubes tall, so the big cube must be at least 3 by 3 by 3, which is $3 \times 3 \times 3 = 27$ small cubes.

Edgar has used 8 cubes: the 3 in the tower and 5 more on the bottom layer. He must add $27 - 8 = 19$.

**Answer: (C) 19**

kangaroo-ca-2019-g0304-10.title: Layer by layer
kangaroo-ca-2019-g0304-10.body:
A 3 by 3 by 3 cube has 3 layers of 9 cubes. Bottom layer: 6 cubes are there (5 plus the bottom of the tower), so 3 are missing. Middle layer: 1 cube is there, 8 missing. Top layer: 1 cube is there, 8 missing. $3 + 8 + 8 = 19$.

**Answer: (C) 19**

kangaroo-ca-2019-g0304-11.title: Two square numbers
kangaroo-ca-2019-g0304-11.body:
A square area uses a square number of tiles: 1, 4, 9, 16, 25, … We need two of them that add up to 25. Only $9 + 16 = 25$ works ($1 + 24$, $4 + 21$ and $25 + 0$ fail, because 24 and 21 are not square numbers and each area needs at least one tile).

The larger area needs $16 - 9 = 7$ more tiles.

**Answer: (C) 7**

kangaroo-ca-2019-g0304-11.title: Think of the sides
kangaroo-ca-2019-g0304-11.body:
The squares are 3 by 3 (9 tiles) and 4 by 4 (16 tiles). The 4 by 4 square is the 3 by 3 square plus an L-shaped strip of $3 + 3 + 1 = 7$ tiles.

**Answer: (C) 7**

kangaroo-ca-2019-g0304-14.title: Read the right balance
kangaroo-ca-2019-g0304-14.body:
On the right balance, the two dogs are lower than the 20 kg weight, so two dogs weigh more than 20 kg, and one dog weighs more than 10 kg. We also know one dog weighs less than 12 kg (the left balance shows this too).

A whole number bigger than 10 and smaller than 12 is 11.

**Answer: (E) 11 kg**

kangaroo-ca-2019-g0304-14.title: Test the choices
kangaroo-ca-2019-g0304-14.body:
12 kg is not less than 12. With 8, 9 or 10 kg, two dogs would weigh at most 20 kg and could not be heavier than the 20 kg weight. 11 kg works: two dogs weigh 22 kg.

**Answer: (E) 11 kg**

kangaroo-ca-2019-g0304-18.title: Count the fives
kangaroo-ca-2019-g0304-18.body:
Up to 49 the digit 5 appears 5 times (5, 15, 25, 35, 45). Pages 50 to 54 add 5 more (10), page 55 adds 2 (12), and pages 56 to 59 add 4 (16).

Pages 60 to 64 have no 5, but page 65 would give the 17th five. So the book has at most 64 pages.

**Answer: (B) 64**

kangaroo-ca-2019-g0304-18.title: Check the choices
kangaroo-ca-2019-g0304-18.body:
49 pages: only 5 fives. 64 pages: 6 fives in the ones place (5, 15, 25, 35, 45, 55) and 10 in the tens place (50–59) = 16 ✓. 66, 74 and 80 pages all include page 65, so there would be at least 17 fives.

**Answer: (B) 64**

kangaroo-ca-2019-g0304-19.title: Measure each part
kangaroo-ca-2019-g0304-19.body:
The bottom part is 8 m wide, so the dashed line is 4 m from its walls. The upright part is $40 - 36 = 4$ m wide, so the line runs 2 m from its walls, at 38 m from the left end. The top part is 6 m wide, so the line is 3 m from its walls.

- Bottom stretch: $40 - 2 = 38$ m.
- Upright stretch: the top part begins 20 m above the bottom wall, so the line goes from 4 m up to $20 + 3 = 23$ m: 19 m.
- Top stretch: $28 - 2 = 26$ m.

Total: $38 + 19 + 26 = 83$ m.

**Answer: (E) 83**

kangaroo-ca-2019-g0304-19.title: Horizontal plus vertical
kangaroo-ca-2019-g0304-19.body:
Horizontal parts: $38 + 26 = 64$ m. Vertical part: $20 + 3 - 4 = 19$ m. Altogether $64 + 19 = 83$ m.

**Answer: (E) 83**

kangaroo-ca-2019-g0304-21.title: Alek and Edek disagree
kangaroo-ca-2019-g0304-21.body:
Alek says he did not eat the cookie, and Edek says Alek did. One of them must be lying. Since only one child lies, everyone else tells the truth, so Bartek's statement is true: Bartek ate the cookie. (Check: then only Edek lies.)

**Answer: (B) Bartek**

kangaroo-ca-2019-g0304-21.title: Try each child
kangaroo-ca-2019-g0304-21.body:
Alek ate it: Alek and Bartek lie ✗. Bartek: only Edek lies ✓. Czarek: Bartek and Edek lie ✗. Darek: Bartek, Darek and Edek lie ✗. Edek: Bartek, Czarek and Edek lie ✗.

**Answer: (B) Bartek**

kangaroo-ca-2019-g0304-22.title: Find the faces
kangaroo-ca-2019-g0304-22.body:
The net has a column 2 squares wide and 4 squares tall: these are the 4 long faces (each 2 squares) going around the box. The two single squares sticking out at the sides are the two small end faces, and both are white.

So the ends of the box are white, which rules out (A) and (C) (red end).

Going around the box, the long faces are: red–blue, blue–blue, blue–red, white–red. A white square appears only on the face white–red, so a long face showing white next to blue, as in (D) and (E), is impossible.

(B) shows the face blue–red in front and the face blue–blue on top; these two faces are neighbours in the net, so (B) is right.

**Answer: (B)**

kangaroo-ca-2019-g0304-22.title: Count colours
kangaroo-ca-2019-g0304-22.body:
The net has 3 red, 4 blue and 3 white squares. The two end squares are white, so only one white square is on the long faces, and it lies next to a red square. In (D) and (E), a white square on a long face lies next to blue, so they are wrong. (A) and (C) have a red end, which is impossible. Only (B) is left.

**Answer: (B)**

kangaroo-ca-2019-g0304-23.title: Where the girls meet
kangaroo-ca-2019-g0304-23.body:
Each girl's first bead slides furthest along her thread, so the beads of the two girls meet in the middle with Ann's first bead (a square) next to Eve's first bead (a star).

Going outward from the meeting point, Ann's side reads square, circle, triangle, star, square, … and Eve's side reads star, circle, triangle, square, star, …

So the piece must contain a square next to a star, with circle, triangle, … continuing on the square's side and circle, triangle, … on the star's side.

(E) is circle, star, square, circle, triangle: from the star-square meeting point, Eve's side goes star, circle ✓ and Ann's side goes square, circle, triangle ✓.

**Answer: (E)**

kangaroo-ca-2019-g0304-23.title: Rule out the others
kangaroo-ca-2019-g0304-23.body:
(C) has no square next to a star, so it can't show the meeting point. In (A), the star next to the square is followed by a triangle, but after Eve's star comes a circle. In (B), the square next to the star is followed by a triangle, but after Ann's square comes a circle. In (D), the star next to the square is followed by a triangle instead of a circle. Only (E) works.

**Answer: (E)**

kangaroo-ca-2019-g0304-24.title: Try short sequences
kangaroo-ca-2019-g0304-24.body:
Start: 1 white, 0 red.

1. White → 5 red: 0 white, 5 red.
2. Red → 9 white: 9 white, 4 red.
3. White → 5 red: 8 white, 9 red.
4. White → 5 red: 7 white, 14 red.

Now $14 = 2 \times 7$. Can it be done in 3 or fewer? After 1 exchange: (0 white, 5 red). After 2: (9 white, 4 red) or nothing else useful (with no white tokens left, only red → white is possible). After 3: (8 white, 9 red) or (17 white, 3 red). None of these has twice as many red as white tokens.

**Answer: (C) 4**

kangaroo-ca-2019-g0304-24.title: Count the changes
kangaroo-ca-2019-g0304-24.body:
Say Anja makes $a$ white→red and $b$ red→white exchanges. Then she has $1 - a + 9b$ white and $5a - b$ red tokens. Red = 2 × white means $5a - b = 2 - 2a + 18b$, so $7a = 2 + 19b$. The smallest solution is $b = 1$, $a = 3$, which is $3 + 1 = 4$ exchanges, and the order above shows it can really be done.

**Answer: (C) 4**
